builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted model uses more compute or memory than your workload can justify.
builder_plan.change: Check for a usable pruned checkpoint and runtime support before attempting model surgery.
builder_plan.baseline: The original unpruned model at the same precision, context, and load.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task quality, actual GPU memory, serving throughput, and preparation cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: NoveltyGate: Novelty, Not Error, Decides Which VLA Prefix Tokens to Compute Exactly
summary: NoveltyGate replaces full-precision MLP computation for all VLA prefix tokens with per-layer routing that sends most tokens through a low-rank MLP and computes exactly only those whose inputs fall outside the calibration subspace, with static shapes enabling a single CUDA graph. It costs a calibration step to estimate the seen subspace, added routing complexity, and reliance on the finding that novelty, not approximation error, predicts which tokens the policy depends on. It can fail if the calibration distribution does not match deployment inputs, if the error-reliance gap does not hold for a different VLA model or camera configuration, or if the 1.61x prefix speedup translates to a smaller end-to-end gain once non-prefix compute dominates.
rationale: The method is training-free and directly reduces per-step VLA inference cost on a single GPU, but it is demonstrated on a single model and benchmark, so its routing calibration and gains require validation on the reader's own policy and workload.
technique: Novelty-based token routing for low-rank VLA MLPs

claims.statement: NoveltyGate replaces full-precision MLP computation for all VLA prefix tokens with per-layer routing that sends most tokens through a low-rank MLP and computes exactly only those whose inputs fall outside the calibration subspace, with static shapes enabling a single CUDA graph. It costs a calibration step to estimate the seen subspace, added routing complexity, and reliance on the finding that novelty, not approximation error, predicts which tokens the policy depends on. It can fail if the calibration distribution does not match deployment inputs, if the error-reliance gap does not hold for a different VLA model or camera configuration, or if the 1.61x prefix speedup translates to a smaller end-to-end gain once non-prefix compute dominates.
Up to 1.61x speedup of the π_0.5 prefix on LIBERO, with action deviation 2.7-2.9x smaller than channel pruning or low-rank compression at equal compute, and preserved closed-loop task success.
